title: The Tale of the King’s Son and the She-Ghoul

paragraphs.en: Once upon a time, there was a king's son who loved hunting. His father appointed a vizier to accompany him on his expeditions. One day, while in the wilderness, the prince chased a beast and lost its trail, finding himself alone.
paragraphs.zh: 从前，有一位国王的儿子酷爱狩猎。他的父亲任命了一位首相陪同他外出打猎。一天，在荒野中，王子追逐一只野兽，却失去了它的踪迹，发现自己孤身一人。

paragraphs.en: He encountered a weeping girl, who told him she was an Indian princess who had fallen off her horse and was now lost.
paragraphs.zh: 他遇到了一个哭泣的女孩，女孩告诉他她是印度的公主，骑马时不慎摔下，现在迷路了。

paragraphs.en: Moved by her plight, the prince took her under his protection. As they passed ruins, the girl requested to relieve herself inside them. The prince obliged, but when he entered after her, he discovered she was a she-ghoul, feeding on human flesh.
paragraphs.zh: 怜悯于她的遭遇，王子收留了她，并给予保护。当他们经过一片废墟时，女孩请求在其中方便。王子答应了，可当他跟进后，却发现她竟是一只雌鬼，正在吞噬人类的肉身。

paragraphs.en: Terrified, the prince fled outside, and the ghoul pursued him.
paragraphs.zh: 惊恐之下，王子逃到了外面，而那个女妖紧随其后。

paragraphs.en: The ghoul asked why he was afraid, and he recounted his ordeal. She advised him to seek help from God. The prince looked up to heaven in prayer.
paragraphs.zh: 女妖问他为何害怕，他便讲述了自己所经历的种种。她建议他向神求助。王子抬头向上帝祈祷。

paragraphs.en: That night, Shahrazad paused her story as dawn approached. Her sister Dinarzad praised it, saying it was strange yet lovely. Shahrazad promised a more amazing tale the next night.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，当黎明渐渐逼近时，沙赫拉兹阿德暂停了她的讲述。她妹妹丁娜兹阿德称赞这个故事既奇异又迷人。沙赫拉兹阿德承诺第二天晚上会带来更加令人惊叹的故事。

paragraphs.en: The following evening, Dinarzad urged Shahrazad to continue. Shahrazad began: She heard that the vizier had spoken to King Yunan about the prince's adventure and the ghoul encounter.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹达催促沙赫拉扎德继续讲述。沙赫拉扎德说道：她听说 vizier 已经和国王尤那讨论过王子的冒险经历以及与女妖的遭遇。

paragraphs.en: The young prince approached the she-ghoul and said he had been unfairly treated. She advised him to pray to God for protection. He did so, asking for help against his enemy.
paragraphs.zh: 年轻的王子走近女妖，说他受到了不公正的对待。女妖建议他向神祈祷求保护。于是他照做了，祈求神明帮助对抗他的敌人。

paragraphs.en: Upon hearing this, the she-ghoul left, allowing the prince to return safely to his father.
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，女妖离开了，王子安全地回到了父亲身边。

paragraphs.en: King Yunan summoned the vizier after learning of the encounter. The vizier warned that trusting and befriending sages could lead to their destruction. He accused the sage Duban of being a foreign agent sent to harm the king.
paragraphs.zh: 云安王得知此事后召见了首相。首相警告说，信任和结交贤士可能会导致他们的背叛，并指责贤士杜班是受外敌派遣来危害国王的间谍。

paragraphs.en: The king agreed, recalling how the sage had cured him externally with something he held.
paragraphs.zh: 国王同意了，回想起那位智者曾用他手中的某种东西为他进行了外治。

paragraphs.en: The king asked the vizier what to do. The vizier suggested killing the sage immediately. King Yunan agreed and summoned Sage Duban, who arrived happily due to recent favors from the king.
paragraphs.zh: 国王问首相该怎么做。首相建议立刻处决那位贤者。云安王同意了，于是召见了得到近期不少恩惠的杜班贤者，杜班欣然前来。

paragraphs.en: Upon entering, Duban recited verses expressing gratitude for gifts received before being asked.
paragraphs.zh: 进入后，杜班在被询问之前先朗读了几句表达感激之情的诗句。

paragraphs.en: The king asked the sage, "Why did I bring you here to be executed?" The sage replied, "I do not know." The king declared, "You are a spy and will die today before you can kill me.
paragraphs.zh: 国王对智者说：“我为什么要把你带来处决？”智者回答：“我不知道。”国王断然说道：“你是个间谍，今天死定了，不会等到你杀我的时候了。”

paragraphs.en: 'Lunch first,' as they say." He then ordered the executioner to kill the sage.
paragraphs.zh: “先吃午饭，”他们常说的。“然后他命令行刑人处死那位智者。

paragraphs.en: Realizing his fate, the sage thought, "Only God can help now; I was rewarded with evil for good deeds." As the king shouted orders, the sage pleaded, "Spare me and you will be spared by God. Destroy me, and God will destroy you."
paragraphs.zh: 意识到自己的命运，智者心想：“如今唯有上帝能助我了；善有善报，恶有恶报，我行善却遭此劫难。”国王下令如潮，智者哀求道：“饶恕我吧，你也会得到上帝的宽恕。毁灭我，上帝也会毁灭你。”

paragraphs.en: King Yunan said, "You must die, sage, as a mere handle cured me, and anything could kill me now." The sage responded, "This is your evil reward for good deeds." The king insisted, "Die today without delay."
paragraphs.zh: 云安王说道：“你必须死，圣贤啊。一个普通的药剂就能救我一命，现在任何东西都能要了我的命。”圣贤回应道：“这是你行善得好报的恶果。”国王坚持道：“今天就让我死吧，不要拖延。”

paragraphs.en: Tears filled the sage's eyes as he mourned his fate. He recited:
paragraphs.zh: 智者的眼中泪光闪烁，为自己的命运哀伤不已。他吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: "Maimuna was a foolish girl, Though from a sage descended. Many with pretense to skill Are many on dry land upended."
paragraphs.zh: “梅伊穆娜是个愚蠢的姑娘，尽管她的祖先不乏智者。许多自诩有才的人，在现实面前纷纷败下阵来。”

paragraphs.en: The executioner approached the sage, bandaged his eyes, bound his hands, and raised the sword. The sage cried out, begging for mercy: "For God's sake, your Majesty, spare me, and God will spare you; destroy me, and God will destroy you." He then began to recite:
paragraphs.zh: 刽子手走近智者，蒙住了他的眼睛，绑住了双手，高举利剑。智者哀求道：“陛下，求求您，为了上帝，请饶恕我吧；饶恕我，上帝也会饶恕您；惩罚我，上帝也会惩罚您。”随后他开始吟诵：

paragraphs.en: "They who deceive enjoy success, While I with my true counsel fail And am rewarded with disgrace. If I live, I'll nothing unveil; If I die, then curse all the men, The men who counsel and prevail."
paragraphs.zh: 欺诈者总能得逞， 而我秉持真心劝谏， 却落得耻辱的下场。 若我活着，绝不多言； 若我死去，只咒骂那些 听信谗言、得势的人。

paragraphs.en: He added, "Is this my reward from your Majesty? It is like the reward of the crocodile." The king asked about the crocodile story.
paragraphs.zh: 他补充道：“这就是我从陛下这里得到的回报吗？这就像鳄鱼得到的奖赏一样。”国王于是询问起了鳄鱼的故事。

paragraphs.en: The sage wept bitterly, repeating his plea for mercy.
paragraphs.zh: 圣人痛哭流涕，反复恳求饶命。

paragraphs.en: Several noblemen approached the king, begging forgiveness for the sage: "We beg your Majesty to spare him for our sake; in our view, he has done nothing deserving this." The king replied that if he spared the sage, he would surely perish, fearing the sage could kill him with anything. He insisted on execution.
paragraphs.zh: 几位贵族走近国王，为那位贤者求情：“恳请您宽恕他吧；依我们看，他并没有犯下如此罪行。”国王回答说，如果饶了那贤者，自己必定难逃一死，因为担心贤者会用任何手段加害于他。国王坚持要将贤者处决。

paragraphs.en: The sage pleaded again, asking for a delay until he could return home and settle his affairs. He requested to donate his scientific and medical books, especially "The Secret of Secrets," which contained countless secrets, including that if the king opened it on the sixth leaf, read three lines from the left page, and spoke to him, his head would answer any question.
paragraphs.zh: 圣人再次恳求，希望能暂时延期，让他回家处理一些事务。他请求将自己所有的科学和医学书籍捐赠出去，特别是那本《秘密中的秘密》，书中蕴含无数的秘密，其中记载：如果国王在第六页打开这本书，在左边一页读三行文字，并对他说话，他的头就会回答任何问题。

paragraphs.en: The king demanded to know the secret but the sage refused to reveal it. The king insisted: "I must kill you."
paragraphs.zh: 国王要求知道这个秘密，但智者拒绝透露。国王坚持说道：“我一定要杀了你。”

paragraphs.en: The king was amazed by the sage Duban's claim. "If I cut off your head and place it on a platter with powder, then read from this old book, will you speak to me?" The king allowed Duban to go home under guard.
paragraphs.zh: 国王对达班圣人的话感到惊讶。“如果我砍下你的头，放在装有粉末的盘子里，然后念诵这部古书的内容，你会和我说话吗？”在士兵的护送下，达班被允许回家了。

paragraphs.en: The next day, Duban returned to the palace, where he found assembled princes, viziers, chamberlains, military officers, and many citizens.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，杜班回到王宫，只见聚集了王子、首相、内臣、军官以及许多市民。

paragraphs.en: Duban entered carrying an old book and a jar of powder. He sat down, ordered a platter, and spread the powder on it. "Take this book," he said to the king, "and don't open it until after my execution.
paragraphs.zh: 杜班抱着一本旧书和一罐粉末走进来，坐下后吩咐上了一大盘子。他把粉末铺在盘子里，对国王说：“你拿着这本书，等我处决后再打开。”

paragraphs.en: When I am beheaded, place my head on the powder and ask questions; it will answer you." The king replied, "I must kill you to see if your head can speak."
paragraphs.zh: “等我被斩首后，把我的头放在粉末上提问，它会回答你。”国王答道：“我必须先把你砍头，才能验证你的头是否真的能说话。”

paragraphs.en: The king ordered the executioner to cut off Duban's head. With one stroke, the sword dropped the head onto the platter. Pressing the head into the powder stopped the bleeding.
paragraphs.zh: 国王命令刽子手割下杜班的头颅。一刀下去，脑袋应声落地，落在了盘子里。将脑袋按进粉末中止住了流血。

paragraphs.en: Duban opened his eyes and said, "Now, open the book." The king did so but found the pages stuck. He wetted his finger with saliva to turn them.
paragraphs.zh: 杜班睁开眼睛，说道：“现在，打开书。”国王照做了，却发现书页粘在一起。他用唾液润湿了手指，才勉强翻开了一页。

paragraphs.en: After turning seven pages, he saw nothing written inside. "Sage," he exclaimed, "there is nothing here." Duban urged him to continue.
paragraphs.zh: 翻了七页后，里面竟然一片空白。“贤者，”他脱口而出，“这里什么也没有。”杜班催促他再接着翻。

paragraphs.en: But as the king turned more pages, a drug from the book began to affect him, causing him to heave and twitch.
paragraphs.zh: 但随着国王翻阅书页，书中似乎有一种魔力开始影响他，让他不由自主地抽搐起来。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged her sister Shahrazad, "Please tell us a tale to pass the time." The king chimed in, asking for the continuation of the sage's story. Shahrazad agreed with enthusiasm.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达催促她的妹妹沙赫拉兹黛：“请你给我们讲个故事打发时间吧。”国王也加入了进来，请求继续讲述智者的故事情节。沙赫拉兹黛满心欢喜地答应了。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O King, that when Sage Duban saw the drug's effect on the king, he recited these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 我听闻，国王啊，当智者杜班看到那药物对国王的影响时，他吟诵了这几行诗句：

paragraphs.en: For long they ruled us arbitrarily, But suddenly vanished their powerful rule. Had they been just, they would have happily Lived, but they oppressed, and punishing fate Afflicted them with ruin deservedly.
paragraphs.zh: 他们 longtime 来任意统治，但突然间强大的统治权便消失了。如果他们公正无私，定会心甘情愿地继续统治下去；然而他们压迫百姓，最终自食其果，遭到了应有的惩罚。

paragraphs.en: As his head finished speaking, both the king and Sage Duban died. Demon, consider this story.
paragraphs.zh: 话音刚落，国王和智者杜班便同时去世。妖魔，请听这个故事。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what an entertaining tale!" Shahrazad replied, "This is nothing compared to what I will tell you tomorrow night if I live."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德沉默下来。丁纳扎德remarked道：“姐姐，这故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答说：“比起我明天晚上要讲的，这简直不算什么。”

paragraphs.en: The next evening, Dinarzad again asked her sister for a tale. The king requested the continuation of the fisherman and demon's story. Shahrazad readily agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达再次向她姐姐请求一个故事。国王要求继续讲述渔夫和妖魔的故事。沙赫拉扎德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman told the demon, "If the king had spared the sage, God would have spared him. But the king insisted on destroying the sage, so God destroyed him. Similarly, if you had spared me from the start, I would have saved you.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫对妖魔说：“如果国王不杀害那位贤者，上帝也不会让他丧命。但国王坚持要除掉贤者，所以上帝也惩罚了他。同样，如果你一开始就放过我，我也能救你一命。”

paragraphs.en: You refused and tried to kill me, so I will punish you by keeping you in this jar and throwing you into the sea." The demon pleaded, "Fisherman, don't do it. Spare me and forgive my actions.
paragraphs.zh: 你拒绝了，还试图杀了我，所以我要把你关在这个罐子里，然后把你扔进海里。”妖魔哀求道：“渔夫，不要这样做。饶恕我吧，原谅我的所作所为。”

paragraphs.en: As they say, 'Be kind to him who wrongs you.' Don’t follow Imama’s example with Atika." The fisherman asked, "What did Imama do to Atika?"
paragraphs.zh: 正如他们所说，“以德报怨”，不要效仿伊马马对待阿蒂卡的方式。“渔夫问道：“伊马马对阿蒂卡做了什么？”

paragraphs.en: The demon replied, "Not now; this place is too small for a story. I will tell you later if you release me."
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔回答说：“现在不行，这里太狭小不适合讲故事。等你放了我，再告诉你吧。”

paragraphs.en: The fisherman said, "I must throw you into the sea. There's no way I'll let you out. You refused my pleas and insisted on killing me without any just cause.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫说道：“我必须把你扔进海里。无论如何我也不会让你活着出去的。你无理拒绝我的请求，竟毫无理由地要置我于死地。”

paragraphs.en: Now that I see your true nature, I will build a hut here to remind anyone who frees you of what you did to me." The demon offered, "Release me this time, and I promise not to bother or harm you. Instead, I'll make you rich."
paragraphs.zh: 既然看穿了你的真面目，我在这里建个小屋，好让任何释放你的人记住你对我做了什么。恶魔提议道：“这次放了我，保证不再骚扰或伤害你，反而会让你变得富有。”

paragraphs.en: Hearing this, the fisherman made the demon pledge: if released, he would not harm but serve the fisherman.
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，渔夫让妖怪发誓：如果放了它，它不仅不会伤害自己，还会为渔夫效劳。

paragraphs.en: After securing the demon's pledge by making him swear by the Almighty Name, the fisherman opened the jar. Smoke rose until it transformed into a full-fledged demon who kicked the jar away, sending it flying to the middle of the sea. The fisherman, fearing disaster, wet himself and summoned his courage.
paragraphs.zh: 在渔夫以神圣之名迫使妖魔立下誓言之后，他打开了那个瓶子。烟雾升腾，最终化作一个完整的妖魔。那妖魔一脚将瓶子踢飞，直奔大海中央。渔夫见状大惊失色，尿意顿生，但他还是鼓足勇气。

paragraphs.en: "Demon," he cried, "you have sworn and given me your pledge. Don’t betray me; come back or face God’s punishment." He repeated the sage Duban's words: "Spare me, and God will spare you; destroy me, and God will destroy you."
paragraphs.zh: “妖魔，”他喊道，“你已发誓并给我作出了承诺。不要背叛我，回来吧，否则将面临上帝的惩罚。”他又重复了圣者杜班的话：“饶恕我，上帝也会饶恕你；毁灭我，上帝也会毁灭你。”

paragraphs.en: The demon laughed, then commanded the fisherman to cast his net in the lake. Miraculously, the lake was filled with colorful fish—white, red, blue, and yellow. The fisherman caught four of them: one of each color.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔笑了，然后命令渔夫在湖中撒网。奇迹般地，湖里出现了色彩斑斓的鱼——白的、红的、蓝的和黄的。渔夫捕到了四条：每种颜色一条。

paragraphs.en: "Take these to your king," the demon instructed, "and he will reward you richly. I know no other way to make you wealthy." He warned the fisherman not to fish more than once a day before disappearing into the ground.
paragraphs.zh: “把这些送给国王，”恶魔吩咐道，“他会重重地奖赏你。我别无他法让你变得富有。”他对渔夫叮嘱了一句不要一天出海捕鱼超过一次后，便消失在了地下。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman returned to the city, marveling at his encounter and the colorful fish. He entered the royal palace and offered the fish to King Yunan. The king examined them closely.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫回到城里，对这次奇遇和五彩斑斓的鱼儿感到十分惊讶。他走进王宫，将鱼献给了云安王。国王仔细端详了一番。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused her tale. Dinarzad exclaimed, "Sister, what an amazing story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more tales to share if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙海拉罕暂停了故事。丁尔扎德脱口而出：“姐姐，这真是个惊人的故事！”沙海拉罕回答道：“要听更多故事，还得等到明天晚上；只要国王不杀我，我就继续讲。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad told Shahrazad, "Sister, tell us what happened to the fisherman." Shahrazad replied, "With pleasure."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达对沙赫拉扎德说：“妹妹，给我们讲讲那个渔夫的经历吧。”沙赫拉扎德回答道：“我很乐意。”

paragraphs.en: When the king received the colored fish from the fisherman, he was amazed. He instructed his vizier to give them to the cook. The vizier then reported back and rewarded the fisherman with four hundred dirhams.
paragraphs.zh: 当国王收到渔夫送来的彩色鱼时，他大为惊讶。他吩咐首相把这些鱼交给厨师。首相随后回报，并赏给渔夫四百第纳尔作为奖励。

paragraphs.en: Overjoyed, the fisherman ran home, tripping and stumbling as if in a dream.
paragraphs.zh: fishermen兴奋不已，跑回家去，仿佛在梦中一般，跌跌撞撞。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the girl prepared the fish by scaling, cleaning, and cutting them into pieces. She heated sesame oil in a pan and fried the fish. Suddenly, the kitchen wall split open, revealing a beautiful maiden with dark eyes, smooth cheeks, and perfect features.
paragraphs.zh: Meanwhile，女孩将鱼清洗干净后切成块。她在锅里加热芝麻油，煎炸着鱼肉。突然，厨房的墙裂开了一道口子，露出一个有着深邃眼睛、光滑脸颊和完美五官的美丽女子。

paragraphs.en: Wearing an Egyptian-style silk shirt embroidered with lace and gold spangles, she held a bamboo wand. The maiden asked the fish if they had kept their pledge. When the cook saw this, she fainted.
paragraphs.zh: 她身穿一件绣有蕾丝和金片的埃及风格丝绸衬衫，手持一根竹杖。少女问鱼儿是否守住了承诺。这时，厨师看到这一幕，不禁昏了过去。

paragraphs.en: The maiden repeated her question, and the fish responded in clear Arabic, affirming that they would return if called upon. She then overturned the pan and vanished as suddenly as she appeared, closing the wall behind her.
paragraphs.zh: 少女再次问道，那条鱼用清晰的阿拉伯语回答说，如果被召唤，它们会回来的。随后她掀开锅盖消失得和出现一样突然，并且随手关上了身后的墙。

paragraphs.en: When the cook regained consciousness, she found the fish charred and felt both sorry for herself and afraid of the king. Remonstrating with her thoughts, she heard a vizier's voice demanding the fish. The girl wept and told him what had happened.
paragraphs.zh: 当厨师恢复知觉时，她发现鱼已经被烧焦了，不禁为自己感到惋惜，同时也害怕国王会因此责罚她。她内心自责地想着，突然听到一个首相的声音在催促她交出那条鱼。女孩哭着告诉对方事情的经过。

paragraphs.en: Astonished, the vizier sent an officer to fetch the fisherman.
paragraphs.zh: 惊异之下，首相派了一名官员去叫来渔夫。

paragraphs.en: The fisherman returned with four more fish. After threats, he went home, took his fishing gear, and ventured outside the city. Climbing a mountain, he descended into the wilderness where he found four charred fish in his net.
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫又带回了四条鱼。经过一番威胁，他回到了家中，拿上钓鱼工具，再次冒险出了城。爬上一座山后，他进入荒野，在网中发现了四条焦黑的鱼。

paragraphs.en: He brought them back, and the vizier instructed the girl to fry them for him.
paragraphs.zh: 他把这些东西带了回来，首相吩咐女孩为他煎炒一番。

paragraphs.en: The wall split open, revealing the she-ghoul in elegant attire, holding a bamboo wand. She repeated her question: "Have you kept your pledge?" The fish answered affirmatively, promising their return if she returned.
paragraphs.zh: 墙突然裂开，露出一位身着华丽服饰的女妖精，手中握着一根竹杖。她再次问道：“你是否遵守了诺言？”那条鱼肯定地点了点头，并承诺如果女妖返回，他们将重归水底。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad praised the story, to which Shahrazad replied that it was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night if she lived.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙海拉兹沉默下来。丁纳扎德称赞起这个故事，沙海拉兹则回应说，这比起她第二天晚上要讲的故事简直不值一提，如果她还能活到那个时候的话。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Dinarzad asked her sister for a tale. With pleasure, Shahrazad agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，迪纳兹达向她的姐姐请求一个故事。沙赫拉扎德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: The vizier informed the king that the maiden had vanished after using her wand to overturn the frying pan. The king wished to see this himself and ordered the fisherman to bring four more fish, which he did—red, white, blue, and yellow. The king instructed the vizier to fry them in his presence.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 告诉国王，那位少女使用魔杖翻转了煎锅后便消失不见了。国王想亲眼看看这一幕，命令渔夫再带来四条鱼——红的、白的、蓝的和黄的。国王吩咐 vizier 在他面前将这些鱼煎熟。

paragraphs.en: The vizier prepared a stove and frying pan, lit the fire, and poured sesame oil. As the fish were nearly ready, the palace wall split open, causing both men to tremble. A tall black slave appeared, as large as a mountain or a giant from the tribe of 'Ad.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 准备了炉子和锅，点燃了火，并倒了些芝麻油。鱼快做好时，宫殿的墙突然裂开，两人不禁打了个寒战。一个高大的黑奴出现了，身材魁梧，仿佛一座山或是‘阿德’部落的巨人。

paragraphs.en: He held a green palm leaf and asked the fish if they had kept their pledge. The fish confirmed that they would return if he did.
paragraphs.zh: 他手里拿着一片绿叶，问鱼儿们是否遵守了诺言。鱼儿们确认说，如果他能回来，他们自然会再来。

paragraphs.en: The black slave overturned the frying pan in the middle of the hall, turning the fish into charcoal before vanishing. The king could not sleep, suspecting a mystery behind these events, and ordered the fisherman to be brought back.
paragraphs.zh: 黑奴在大厅中间翻倒了煎锅，活蹦乱跳的鱼瞬间化作了木炭，随后便消失不见了。国王辗转难眠，怀疑这其中藏着什么玄机，于是下令将渔夫重新叫了回来。

paragraphs.en: Upon the fisherman's arrival, the king asked, "Where do you catch such strange fish?" The fisherman replied, "My lord, I find them in a lake among four hills on the other side of the mountain." The vizier admitted ignorance: "Your Majesty, I have never seen or heard of this lake despite my extensive travels for sixty years."
paragraphs.zh: 渔夫一到，国王问道：“你怎么捕到这么奇怪的鱼？”渔夫回答说：“陛下，我在山那边四座小山环抱的一个湖里发现它们。”首相承认自己不知情：“陛下，尽管我六十年来四处奔波，也从未见过或听说过这个湖泊。”

paragraphs.en: The king then questioned the distance. "How far is it?" The fisherman answered, "It's just one hour from here."
paragraphs.zh: 国王接着询问距离：“到底有多远？”渔夫回答说：“从这里出发，只需一个小时的路程。”

paragraphs.en: Astonished, the king ordered his soldiers to prepare and rode out with them behind the fisherman.
paragraphs.zh: 国王惊讶不已，立刻命令士兵们准备妥当，随后与他们一同骑马出发，跟随渔夫身后。

paragraphs.en: They ascended the mountain and descended to a vast wilderness they had never seen before. There were four hills and a lake where colorful fish swam: red, white, blue, and yellow. The king was amazed and turned to his courtiers.
paragraphs.zh: 他们登上山顶，然后来到一片从未见过的广阔荒野。这里有四座小山和一个湖，湖里游弋着色彩斑斓的鱼：红的、白的、蓝的和黄的。国王惊叹不已，转头对随从们说道。

paragraphs.en: "Has any of you ever seen this lake?" They all replied, "Never."
paragraphs.zh: “你们中有谁见过这个湖吗？”他们齐声回答说：“从来没有。”

paragraphs.en: The king declared, "There must be a mystery here." He vowed not to return until he discovered the truth about the lake and its colorful fish. He ordered his men to halt and set up camp before dismounting to wait.
paragraphs.zh: 国王宣布：“这里一定有蹊跷。”他发誓要查明湖中那些五彩斑斓的鱼儿之谜后才返回。于是命令随从停下，安营扎寨，自己则下马耐心等候。

paragraphs.en: The king summoned his vizier at nightfall. The vizier, wise and experienced, arrived unseen by soldiers. The king instructed him to sit at the tent entrance early next morning, telling princes that he was indisposed and had forbidden anyone from seeing him for three days.
paragraphs.zh: 傍晚时分，国王召见了他的首相。这位首相智勇双全，悄无声息地来到了帐篷前。国王吩咐他在第二天一早坐在帐篷入口处，并告诉王子们他身体不适，接下来三天任何人都不得前来探望。

paragraphs.en: The vizier obeyed.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 遵命行事。

paragraphs.en: Prepared and armed with the royal sword, the king set out alone after dark. He climbed one of four hills and reached the top by night's end. At dawn, sunlight illuminated a distant dark mass.
paragraphs.zh: 备好王剑，国王独自一人夜幕降临后出发。他攀上了四座山丘之一，在夜色尽头抵达山顶。黎明时分，阳光照亮了远处的一片暗影。

paragraphs.en: Excited, he approached it, hoping to find someone who could provide information about the lake and fish. Upon arrival, he found an iron-plate-covered palace built under a lucky star.
paragraphs.zh: 兴奋不已，他走近那地方，希望能找到有人能提供关于湖水和鱼类的信息。到了那里，他发现有一座铁板覆盖的宫殿建在一片吉星高照的土地上。

paragraphs.en: Knocking gently, then louder, without response, the king entered, shouting for inhabitants but receiving no reply. Boldly, he ventured into the center of the empty palace, finding it deserted.
paragraphs.zh: 轻声敲门，随后声音越来越大，但无人应答。国王推门而入，大声喊叫询问是否有居民在内，却得不到任何回应。他大胆地走进空荡荡的宫殿中央，发现这里一片荒凉。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged Shahrazad: "Sister, tell us one of your enchanting tales to pass the time." Shahrazad agreed with pleasure.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达催促沙赫拉扎德：“姐姐，给我们讲一个你那些迷人的故事吧，打发时间。”沙赫拉扎德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: King Shahryar walked through his palace, seeing no one despite its luxurious furnishings—silk carpets, leather mats, and drapes. Settees, benches, and seats with cushions surrounded a spacious courtyard, flanked by four recessed courts. A fountain in the center featured lions made of red gold, spouting water that looked like gems.
paragraphs.zh: 国王沙赫里亚尔漫步在他的宫殿中，尽管装饰豪华——丝织地毯、皮质垫子和窗帘，但偌大一个宫殿空无一人。宽敞的庭院被四座凹室环绕，四周摆放着长沙发、长凳和带垫座椅。中央有一个喷泉，喷泉中的狮子由赤金打造，喷出的水仿佛宝石般璀璨夺目。

paragraphs.en: Singing birds fluttered nearby under a high net.
paragraphs.zh: 高网之下，鸟儿轻快地飞舞歌唱。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, the king heard sad moans and verses: "My soul is torn between peril and toil; O life, dispatch me with one mighty blow." The verses continued, describing a lover's plight.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，国王听到了悲伤的呻吟和诗句：“我的灵魂在危险与劳苦间挣扎；哦，生命，请赐我一击毙命。”接着，诗句继续描述着一个恋人的困境。

paragraphs.en: The king approached the source of the voice, finding a young man sitting on a chair raised about twenty inches above the floor. He was handsome, with a full figure, clear voice, radiant brow, and ruddy cheeks, marked by a mole like amber.
paragraphs.zh: 国王走近声音的来源，发现一个年轻人正坐在一张离地面约五十厘米高的椅子上。他相貌英俊，身材匀称，嗓音清澈悦耳，眉宇间透出一股光彩，脸颊红润，在他的下巴处有一个像琥珀般色泽的痦子。

paragraphs.en: The king greeted a seated young man, pleased to see him. The young man wore an Egyptian silk robe with gold embroidery and an conical head covering, but his face showed signs of grief. He greeted the king courteously, saying he was unworthy of rising.
paragraphs.zh: 国王迎接了一位坐着的年轻人，见他前来十分高兴。这位年轻人身穿绣有金色图案的埃及丝绸长袍，并戴着尖顶帽，但脸上流露出悲伤的痕迹。他礼貌地向国王问候，说自己不配起身相迎。

paragraphs.en: The king asked about the lake, colored fish, and why the young man sat alone in sorrow.
paragraphs.zh: 国王询问起那湖中的景色、五彩斑斓的鱼儿，以及为何那位年轻人独自哀坐。

paragraphs.en: The young man began to weep, reciting Mawwaliya verses: "Say to the man life's arrows pierced; how many have felt fate's blows?" He continued, "If you slept, God watched; who can say time is fair or life constant?"
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人开始哭泣，吟诵着马瓦利亚的诗句：“对那箭矢穿心的人说吧；多少人曾感受到命运的打击？”他继续说道：“如果你睡了，上帝在守护；谁能断言时间是公平的，生活是恒定的？”

paragraphs.en: He then revealed that one half of his body was human flesh from the navel up, while the other half, from the navel down, was black stone. King Shahrayar was astonished and decided to postpone executing Shahrazad for a month.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后披露，从肚脐以上部分是人类的肉身，而从肚脐以下则变成了黑色的石头。国王沙哈拉叶尔大为惊讶，决定将莎赫拉兹德的死刑推迟一个月。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Dinarzad encouraged her sister, saying she had heard an entertaining story. Shahrazad replied that it paled in comparison to what she would tell the next night if she lived.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，迪纳兹鼓励她的妹妹，说她听了一个有趣的故事。沙赫拉扎德回应说，如果她能活到明天晚上，她要讲的故事会更加精彩。

paragraphs.en: The king felt sorrow for the young man and said, "Young man, your troubles add to mine. I sought answers for the fish but now must also find yours. Only God can help us.
paragraphs.zh: 国王怜悯这位年轻人，说道：“年轻人，你的困境让我更加忧心。我本为鱼儿的事四处求解，现在还得为你找到答案。只有上帝能帮助我们。”

paragraphs.en: Tell me your story quickly." The young man replied, "Listen with all your senses."
paragraphs.zh: “快把你的故事告诉我。”年轻人回答说，“用你所有的感官听好。”

paragraphs.en: The king assured him, "I am ready to hear you out." The young man then began his tale.
paragraphs.zh: 国王向他保证：“我愿意洗耳恭听。”年轻人随后开始了他的讲述。

paragraphs.en: He explained that he had been given a cosmetic used by Eastern women to darken their eyelids and small silver coins called dirhams. He mentioned tribes destroyed by God's wrath and poems sung with reed pipes, though these details were not directly relevant to his story.
paragraphs.zh: 他解释说，自己曾使用东方女性用来加深眼睑颜色的化妆品，以及一些被称为第拉姆的小银币。他还提到了因上帝愤怒而被摧毁的部落和用芦笛吹奏的诗歌，尽管这些细节与他的故事关系不大。
